summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM applications move into production, where unpredictable model behavior, latency spikes, and runaway token costs can quietly erode reliability and budgets. Modern observability tools provide distributed tracing with span hierarchies, trace-level replay for debugging, evaluation frameworks, and granular cost tracking so teams can understand, debug, and optimize their AI systems. Without this visibility, diagnosing quality regressions or cost overruns in complex multi-step LLM pipelines is nearly impossible.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces of LLM chains and agents, token usage, latency, cost, evaluation scores, and prompt/response quality.
features: Distributed tracing with span hierarchies for chains and agents
Tight integration with LangChain and LangGraph
tools.pricing: Free tier includes 5,000 monthly traces. Beyond the allowance, base traces (14-day retention) cost $2.50 per 1k and extended traces (400-day retention) cost $5.00 per 1k. Paid Plus plan adds higher limits and seats, with custom enterprise pricing available.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on the LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem who want deeply integrated tracing and evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token usage, cost per request/user/model, latency, caching hits, and error rates via a proxy or async logging.
features: One-line proxy integration for request logging
Granular cost and usage tracking per user, model, and request
Caching to reduce redundant API calls
tools.pricing: Free tier includes 10,000 monthly traces. Pro plan is $79/month (approximately $79 per 100,000 traces), Team plan is $799/month, with custom enterprise pricing available.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting fast, low-effort cost monitoring and caching across any LLM provider with minimal code changes.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces and evaluations (via W&B Weave), model experiments, training runs, token/cost metrics, and production quality.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Strong MLOps integration for the full model lifecycle
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal/individual use. Team and enterprise plans are usage- and seat-based with custom pricing; typically starts around $50/user/month for teams.
tools.best_for: ML teams that need unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability across the full model development lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML model performance, drift, embeddings, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics with root-cause analysis.
features: LLM tracing and evaluation via OpenInference/Phoenix
Open-source Phoenix tool for local tracing and evals
Drift, data quality, and performance monitoring
Embedding and cluster analysis for RAG debugging
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open-source. Arize AX offers a free tier, with Pro and enterprise plans at custom/usage-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade monitoring, drift detection, and RAG/embedding debugging at scale.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, evaluation scores, and prompt performance across any framework.
features: Evaluations, scores, and user feedback capture
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host. Cloud Hobby tier is free with limited traces; Core (~$29/month) and Pro/Team plans scale with usage, plus custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, framework-agnostic observability stack they can self-host for full data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM and vector DB calls, token usage, latency, and cost exported as standard OpenTelemetry traces and metrics.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM providers and frameworks
Vendor-neutral export to any OTel-compatible backend
Integrates with existing observability stacks (Grafana, Datadog, etc.)
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free. Backend/hosting costs depend on the chosen OpenTelemetry destination; Traceloop offers a hosted platform with free and paid usage-based tiers.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation plugged into their existing observability tooling.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar prompts (e.g., with Helicone or prompt caching) to avoid paying for redundant completions.
Route requests intelligently: use smaller, cheaper models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Set token limits, trim context, and compress or summarize long histories to reduce input/output token counts.
Monitor cost per user, feature, and model with observability dashboards and set alerts to catch runaway spend early.
